neet_phy_u14_t05_1.working: For a pure capacitor, i = C dv/dt. With v = V0 sin ωt, i = ωCV0 cos ωt, so the current leads the voltage by π/2.

neet_phy_u14_t05_4.working: XL = ωL (IV). XC = 1/(ωC) (III). Z = √(R² + (XL − XC)²) (I). I0 = V0/Z (II).

neet_phy_u14_t05_5.working: A is true because XL is proportional to f. B is true because XC → ∞ as ω → 0. C is false because the voltages add as phasors, not arithmetically. D is false because an ideal inductor is a short circuit for DC. E is true because XC is proportional to 1/f.
